Interesting! The click on the green block didn't change the gameplay (gameplay_changed=False), and the green block is still there. This is different from before when clicking on green blocks removed them.
Wait, looking at the result more carefully: `gameplay_changed=False` but the green block is still there. This suggests that clicking on this green block didn't remove it.
But earlier, clicking on green blocks at (3,15), (3,21), (3,27), (15,33), (15,39), (15,45), (15,51) removed them. Now clicking on (15,51) didn't remove the green block at (13,49)-(17,53).
Wait, (15,51) is within (13,49)-(17,53), so I should have clicked on the green block. But it didn't remove it.
Hmm, maybe the green block spawned by ACTION7 is different from the initial green blocks. Or maybe there's a cooldown or limit on how many green blocks can be removed.
Let me try clicking on a different position within the green block, or try ACTION7 again to see what happens.
Actually, wait. Let me re-read the result. The click was at (15,51), and the green block is at (13,49)-(17,53). The center of the green block would be around (15,51), so I should have clicked on it.
But the result shows `gameplay_changed=False`, which means the board didn't change. This is strange.
Let me try clicking on the center of the green block more precisely. The boundary is (13,49)-(17,53), so the center is (15,51). But maybe the green block is not a solid block, and I need to click on a specific part of it.
Actually, looking at the earlier green blocks, they had 21 pixels each. A 5x5 block would have 25 pixels, so 21 pixels suggests a 5x5 block with 4 missing pixels (maybe the corners or the center).
Let me try clicking on different positions within the green block to find the clickable area.
But wait, I'm wasting actions. Let me think about this differently.
Maybe the goal is not to remove all green blocks, but to do something else. Let me try moving the player to the right and see if something happens.
Actually, looking at the image, there's a green block at the top right of the sky blue path. Maybe the goal is to move the player to that position and then do something.
But the player is at the bottom left, and the green block is at the top right. The player can only move LEFT/RIGHT, not UP/DOWN.
Let me try a different approach. Let me move the player to the right edge and see if something happens.

        rows = [p[0] for p in b]

        print(f"{n['color']}: ({min(rows)},{min(cols)})-({max(rows)},{max(cols)}), {n['pixels']} pixels")

</function>
